findings.description: Critical: proposal.md What Changes still says 'Coverage disclosure line. Every answer ends with one line… The line is not optional and not collapsible' and treats any non-zero `--check` as 'stale', but adjudicated D5 / skill-workflow 'Explainer Grounding' require `Grounding:` only on sketching replies, exempt ambiguous-symbol clarification (`--tree` exit 3) and whole-repository redirects, and distinguish `graph absent` / `graph check failed` / `graph stale`. An implementer or reviewer reading the proposal gets the pre-adjudication contract.
findings.resolution: Rewrite the Coverage disclosure and Grounding bullets in proposal.md to match D5: disclosure on sketching replies only; name the two exemptions; point at the closed first-match reason set instead of collapsing all failures to 'stale'.

findings.description: Nit: NFR 'Coverage honesty' targets '100% of behavioural-scenario replies, grounded and ungrounded' carrying a disclosure line, but skill-workflow now has behavioural scenarios that MUST NOT include `Grounding:` ('Ambiguous symbol asks instead of guessing', 'Whole-repository redirect has no disclosure line'). The metric contradicts the exempted reply shapes.
findings.resolution: Narrow the NFR to sketching replies (catalogue visual emitted), or to the deterministic disclosure checks in test_behaviour.py, and exclude clarification/redirect replies.

findings.description: Nit: proposal.md Frontmatter bullet says the skill test 'asserts the four surviving keys explicitly', but the declared key set is six (`name`, `description`, `category`, `tags`, `user_invocable`, `related`) — matching D6 and the Frontmatter requirement. 'Four' is a stale count.
findings.resolution: Replace 'four surviving keys' with 'six surviving keys' (or list them) so the proposal matches D6/spec/tasks 2.1.

findings.description: Nit: Explainer Grounding's first-match reason table puts `form not graph-backed` last, but the same requirement also says 'other catalogue forms SHALL use `form not graph-backed`' and the Non-call-tree scenario always expects that reason. If the skill also observes `graph absent`/`graph stale` while answering with a component/file/sequence/structural-diff form, first-match and the form-SHALL disagree on the disclosure token.
findings.resolution: State that catalogue-form selection short-circuits the graph reason chain: non-call-tree sketching replies always use `form not graph-backed`, and the first-match table applies only when the chosen form is a call tree.

findings.description: Nit: The closed ungrounded reason set still leaves `--tree` spawn/OSError (and any `--tree` exit other than 1/2/3) undefined after a fresh `--check`. `graph check failed` covers `--check` spawn failure and `--tree` exit `1` only. 'Stale or absent graph falls back to source' WHEN also omits `--check` spawn failure, yet THEN lists `graph check failed` as a reason — so that token has no dedicated WHEN/THEN for either spawn path.
findings.resolution: Extend `graph check failed` (in D5 + spec) to include failure to spawn/run `--tree`, and add a scenario WHEN `--check` cannot be spawned or `--tree` exits `1`/cannot be spawned after a fresh check THEN disclosure uses `graph check failed`.

findings.description: Nit: Round-2 frontmatter/distribution scenarios remain under-linked in tasks.md Spec scenarios lines. Task 2.1 body asserts no `triggers`, Architecture-related keys, and tail sections, but its Spec scenarios omit 'Frontmatter omits triggers and sets Architecture category' and 'Skill markdown ends with required tail sections'. Task 2.6 lists only 'Manifest validation passes' while omitting 'Manifest declares portable distribution and atlas dependencies'; task 2.5/2.6 never cite 'Sibling skill paths use skill-base-dir form'.
findings.resolution: Extend task 2.1 Spec scenarios with the triggers/category/tail scenarios; extend 2.6 with the portable/deps scenario; attach the skill-base-dir scenario to 2.5 or 2.6.

findings.description: Optional: Atlas target resolution SHALL accepts 'module file path or basename', but the only module scenario is 'File target gives the aggregated module view' with `--tree <file-basename>`. A path-form target (e.g. `skills/foo/bar.py`) has no WHEN/THEN, so path vs basename behaviour is unpinned for implementers.
findings.resolution: Accept if basename coverage is enough for v1, or add a scenario WHEN `--tree` is given a module file path THEN it roots at that module like the basename case.

findings.description: Exit `3` for ambiguous `--tree` targets with ask-don't-guess (no source fallback, no `Grounding:`) is consistently specified across D4/D5, codebase-analysis, and skill-workflow, and task 1.1/2.5 cite the matching scenarios.

Task 1.1 Spec scenarios now enumerate the round-2/3 atlas scenarios (footer shape, resolution precedence, unique name, direction both, defaults/clamp/`--no-coverage`/exit 1) and the exit-3 split, matching codebase-analysis — closing the earlier orphaned-scenario gap for wp-atlas-tree.
